passages.provision_quote: Except for a form produced by the United States election assistance commission, any application for registration shall be accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship as prescribed in section 16-166, subsection F, and the county recorder or other officer in charge of elections shall reject any application for registration that is not accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship.
passages.note: Chapter 99 text prints the operative registration-citizenship provision but names no voter.
Bill overview page for the same instrument; it prints sponsors and governor action, not her act and not the provision.

rows.reasoning: On HB 2492 (2022) she voted No at House Third Reading ("HERNANDEZ A N", "Passed 31-26-3-0-0"), on a bill whose operative section provides that "any application for registration shall be accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship". A No vote rejects "Require documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote" but says nothing about what identification she would require instead, so it separates the sides without choosing among "Require no identification to vote, verifying voters by signature or existing records.", "Accept non-photo identification, such as a utility bill or bank statement.", "Require photo ID to vote, but let voters without one cast a ballot after signing an affidavit." and "Require photo ID in person and an ID number on every mail ballot." Ruling out the top rung is not evidence for any rung below it.
